lead: The card that opens up the whole of Valencia: free transport, 14 museums included, a free tapa and discounts of up to 50% at more than 130 tourist services.
Choose the option that best suits the length and type of your trip.

items.kicker: The most complete · Transport included · Activated on first use
items.title: Valencia Tourist Card 24, 48 and 72 hours
items.subtitle: Free transport · 14 museums and monuments · Tapa with a drink · Discounts up to 50%
items.body: The star option of the Valencia Tourist Card. For 24, 48 or 72 hours it lets you travel free on all EMT city buses and Metrobus metropolitan buses, the metro (zones A and B, with the airport stop included), the tram and Renfe commuter trains in zone AB. It also includes free entry to 14 municipal museums and monuments, discounts of up to 50% at the main tourist attractions — the City of Arts and Sciences, Oceanogràfic, Bioparc, the Tourist Bus, 50% off at the Marqués de Dos Aguas, 20% at the Cathedral — and a free tapa with a drink. The card is activated on first use and is valid continuously from that moment. Also available in 72-hour packs combined with entry to the CAC, the Oceanogràfic and the Bioparc.

items.kicker: For long stays · No transport · Cathedral + IVAM included
items.title: Valencia Tourist Card 7 days without transport
items.subtitle: 7 days of discounts · Free Cathedral · Free IVAM · 14 museums · No daily expiry
items.body: The ideal option for those staying a week in Valencia who don’t need transport included (for example, if they already have a metro pass or get around by bike). It includes free entry to Valencia Cathedral and its Cathedral Museum — where the Holy Chalice is kept — free entry to the IVAM (Institut Valencià d’Art Modern, the best modern art museum in the region), free access to the 14 municipal museums and monuments and discounts of up to 50% at the same attractions as the 24–72 h version. There is also a combined 7-day option with a 24-hour Tourist Bus included.

Where do you buy and collect the Valencia Tourist Card?
items.body: It can be bought online at visitvalencia.com with a 10% discount. It is also sold at the Valencia Tourist Offices (Plaza de la Reina, Estación del Nord, Airport) and at top-up points across the city. The digital version is activated directly on your phone.

items.title: When does the card’s time start counting?
items.body: The card is activated on first use — whether on transport or at the entrance to a museum. From that moment the continuous validity period (24, 48, 72 hours or 7 days) begins.

items.title: Does it include the airport in the transport?
items.body: Yes. The 24/48/72-hour option includes metro zone AB, which covers the Valencia Airport stop (L3 and L5). The airport–centre journey is covered.

items.title: How many times can each discount be used?
items.body: Free access to municipal museums and monuments is once per museum. Discounts at tourist attractions and businesses are per person and per visit, according to the terms of each attraction.

items.title: Is there a card for groups?
items.body: Yes. There is a Valencia Tourist Card for groups, available at visitvalencia.com, with special conditions for organised groups and travel agencies.

blocks.title: Tips to get the most out of the Valencia Tourist Card
items: Always buy on the official visitvalencia.com website: you get a 10% discount that is not available through other channels
The 72-hour option is the best value for most travellers: it covers transport and museums and lets you see the whole city without worrying
If you already have transport covered or get around by bike, the 7-day card includes the Cathedral and the IVAM and works out cheaper
The card covers the airport in the 24/48/72-hour options: you can get from the airport to the centre without paying anything extra
The packs with tickets to the CAC and the Oceanogràfic are the cheapest option if you plan to visit those attractions: the saving compared with buying separately is considerable
The tapa with a drink is valid at selected establishments; check the discount guide at visitvalencia.com for the full list
